title: Scene, scene/0 (draft)
description: What a view draws, with no size: a flat list of shapes in ratios of the part each is in, with stable keys and paint tokens. buildScene() makes one from a plan and a result, and a custom mark's `scene` makes its own. A draft: it says the scene as it is built today, and its names may still change. A node says where it is in the same fields whatever its kind and its layout: x and y where it is, x2 and y2 its other end, w and h an extent. x runs across its box from the start and y up it from the bottom, 0 to 1, in its part's box or, in a list, its row's track. A value may fall outside 0 to 1 where a mark does: a bar below its axis. An arc keeps fields of its own, about its part's centre. The number, a legend, a list's rows and a notice carry no position: a surface sets them in order.

layout.description: cartesian, rows, band, radial, matrix, none, notice or prose, or the name of a custom mark, which is laid out by its own code.

parts.description: The parts the plan shows, with all the room they ask for. Which of them show at a room is the fit rules' to say (fitTo). A scene holds nodes of parts that are not here, for a rule to show in another's place: the number, and both forms of a legend.

rows.description: Dimension values in order: the x domain, the rows, the segments, slices or rings.

series.description: The values of the dimension on color, where a view is split into series. A series' paint is its place here.

detail.description: The values of the dimension on detail, where a view is split into series that are not painted apart.

ys.description: In a grid, the y dimension's values in order.

scale.description: How x is shared among the rows of a plot.

track.description: In rows: the track stands beside the label and the values, because its marks are read by where they are.

aspect.description: Where a part holds its shape, its width over its height.

part.description: A part is a box a surface lays out, and what a fit rule names.

paint.description: A token, never a colour. A surface maps each to its own colours.

oneOf.description: A bar, a segment of a band, a cell, a swatch or a box.

key.description: Stable across renders and unique in the scene. Transitions and keyboard navigation hang on it.

legend.description: Its paint is one of a legend's. Where the legend goes with nothing in its place, the mark is drawn in its layer's own paint.

axis.description: It is on a plot's second y scale, and goes when that axis goes.

row.description: The dimension value the node came from.

series.description: The value it came from of the dimension on color or on detail.

rank.description: Absent stays. A ranked node is given up when room is short, the higher its rank the sooner.

tone.description: A fill that tints and does not mark.

pair.description: The two dimension values a cell or a grid's dot came from: the one on x, then the one on y.

oneOf.description: A line or the fill under one. `d` is drawn in a box of 100 by 100 for a surface to stretch, and `points` are what it was drawn from.
